title: Social News Feed
summary: Design the home timeline of a social network where users follow accounts and see their recent posts newest first — including accounts with tens of millions of followers.
statement:
You are designing **the home feed of a social network**. People publish short posts (up to 500 characters of text plus up to 4 photos) and follow other accounts. Following is one-directional: you can follow a celebrity without them following you back.

**Core journeys**
1. **Post** — a user publishes a post; it shows at the top of their own profile immediately.
2. **Home feed** — a user opens the app and sees posts from the accounts they follow, newest first, 20 at a time, and can keep scrolling back through older posts. Pull-to-refresh shows anything new since the last load.
3. **Follow / unfollow** — following someone makes their recent posts show up in your feed soon after; unfollowing removes them.
4. **Engagement** — every post in the feed shows its like count and comment count, and users can like or unlike posts.
5. **Delete** — an author can delete a post; it should vanish from everybody's feed shortly afterwards.

**Clarifications from the interviewer**
- Ordering is reverse-chronological; no machine-learned ranking for this exercise.
- Most accounts have a few hundred followers, but some athletes, musicians and news outlets have 10–100 million followers and post several times a day.
- A user follows about 200 accounts on average (hard cap: 5,000).
- Many registered users open the app only once a month or less.
- If you block someone, you must never see their posts in your feed.
- Like and comment counts may be a few seconds stale, but your own like must show immediately for you.

Walk through requirements, estimates, API, data model and architecture, and explain the trade-offs behind how a new post reaches its followers' feeds.
scaleHints: 500M monthly active users, 200M daily active users
Each DAU loads the feed ~10 times a day → ~2B feed loads/day (~23K/s on average, ~70K/s at peak)
~20M new posts per day (~230/s on average, ~1K/s at peak); 30% include photos averaging 300 KB each
Average 200 followees per user; follower counts are heavily skewed, up to 100M for the largest accounts
First feed page p99 under 300 ms; new posts appear in followers' feeds within 10 s (within 1 minute for the largest accounts)
constraints: Feeds may be eventually consistent, but authors must see their own posts immediately
Deleted posts and posts from blocked accounts must disappear from feeds within 1 minute
Feed availability (99.95%) matters more than perfect freshness — a slightly stale feed beats an error
Infinite scroll must not repeat or skip posts when new posts arrive while the user is scrolling
outOfScope: Ranking/recommendation models, ads and suggested posts
Comment threads themselves (only counts appear in the feed)
Direct messages, stories, video and search
Notifications about likes or new followers

keyFunctionalRequirements: Create and delete posts (text plus up to 4 photos)
Home feed: reverse-chronological posts from followees with cursor pagination and refresh for newer posts
Like/unlike with counts shown on feed items
Filter blocked accounts and deleted posts
Author's own posts visible immediately on profile and feed
keyNonFunctionalRequirements: Read-heavy: ~70K feed loads/s at peak vs ~1K posts/s — optimise the read path
Feed p99 < 300 ms; post visible to followers within 10 s (1 min for the largest accounts)
Highly available, eventually consistent feeds with read-your-own-writes for authors
Storage-efficient timelines (ids, not post copies) for 200M active users
coreEntities: User: user_id, handle, profile, follower_count, following_count, high-fanout flag
Post: post_id (time-sortable), author_id, text, media_refs, created_at, deleted
Follow: follower_id, followee_id, created_at — indexed in both directions
Timeline entry: user_id → bounded list of (post_id, author_id) for active users
Like: post_id, user_id, created_at; PostCounters: post_id, like_count, comment_count
keyComponents: Post service that persists posts and emits post-created/deleted events
Social graph service answering 'who follows X' and 'whom does Y follow' at scale
Fan-out workers that push post ids into followers' precomputed timelines
Timeline store/cache holding the newest few hundred post ids per active user
Feed service merging the precomputed timeline with on-demand pulls from high-fanout accounts, then hydrating posts
Hydration caches for post bodies, counters and author profiles
Object storage plus edge caching for photos
Counter service for likes/comments with asynchronous aggregation
deepDiveTopics: Fan-out on write vs on read vs hybrid: the follower threshold for celebrities and merging at read time
Timeline sizing: e.g. 200M users × 800 ids × 8 bytes ≈ 1.3 TB, kept only for active users; rebuilding feeds for returning users
Cursor pagination with time-sortable post ids so new posts don't shift pages
Deletes, unfollows and blocks: lazy filtering at read time vs eager removal from timelines
Counters for hot posts: sharded counters, batching likes, caching counts
commonPitfalls: Pure fan-out on write: one 100M-follower post triggers 100M timeline writes
Pure fan-out on read: querying ~200 followees and merging on every load at 70K/s
Offset-based pagination that repeats or skips posts as new ones arrive
Copying full post bodies into every timeline instead of ids
Fanning out to inactive users' timelines, wasting most of the work
Forgetting read-your-own-writes, so authors don't see their own post
